title: Legislative districts of Agusan del Norte

{{Short description|Legislative District of the Philippines}}
{{Politics of the Philippines}}
The '''legislative districts of Agusan del Norte''' are the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Agusan del Norte]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The province is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through its [[Agusan del Norte's 1st congressional district|first]] and [[Agusan del Norte's 2nd congressional district|second congressional districts]].

== History ==
{{further|Legislative districts of Mindanao and Sulu|Legislative districts of Agusan}}
Prior to gaining separate representation, areas now under the jurisdiction of Agusan del Norte were represented under the [[Department of Mindanao and Sulu]] (1917–1935) and [[Agusan (province)|Agusan]] (1935–1969).

Republic Act No. 4979, approved in a plebiscite held simultaneously with the [[1967 Philippine Senate election|1967 elections]], split the old Agusan Province into [[Agusan del Norte]] and [[Agusan del Sur]] and provided them each with a congressional representative.<ref name="RA4979">{{Cite web |last=Congress of the Philippines |date=June 16, 1967 |title=Republic Act No. 4979 - An Act Creating the Provinces of Agusan del Norte and Agusan del Sur |url=https://www.lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1967/ra_4979_1967.html |access-date=February 4, 2017 |website=The LawPhil Project}}</ref> In accordance with Section 7 of R.A. 4979, Agusan del Norte first elected its separate representative starting in the [[1969 Philippine House of Representatives elections|1969 elections]].<ref name=RA4979/> The chartered city of [[Butuan]], despite being enumerated as part of the territory of neither successor province,<ref name=RA4979/> was designated as Agusan del Norte's seat of provincial government and became part of its congressional representation.

Agusan del Norte was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region X]] from 1978 to 1984, and returned one representative to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]].

Under the new Constitution which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987, the [[Agusan del Norte]] was grouped with the highly urbanized city of Butuan and reapportioned into two congressional districts;<ref>{{Cite web |last=1986 Constitutional Commission |date=February 2, 1987 |title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance |url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/ |access-date=November 21, 2017 |website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines}}</ref> each district elected its member to the restored [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]] starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]].

The approval of Republic Act No. 11714 on April 4, 2022, divided the province into two congressional districts: the lone legislative district of the City of Butuan and the lone legislative district of the province of Agusan del Norte,<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=April 4, 2022|title=Republic Act No. 11714 - An Act Reapportioning the Province of Agusan del Norte into the Lone Legislative District of the City of Butuan and the Lone Legislative District of the Province of Agusan del Norte |url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/downloads/2022/04apr/20220427-RA-11714-RRD.pdf |access-date=May 11, 2022 |website=[[Official Gazette (Philippines)]]}}</ref> which elected their separate representatives starting in the [[2025 Philippine House of Representatives elections|2025 elections]].

== Senatorial representation ==
{{further|Philippines's 12th senatorial district}}
Between 1916 and 1935, the territory of what is now Agusan del Norte (then part of the undivided province of [[Agusan (province)|Agusan]]) was represented in the [[Senate of the Philippines]] through the [[Philippines's 12th senatorial district|12th senatorial district of the Philippine Islands]]. However, in 1935, all senatorial districts were abolished when a unicameral [[National Assembly of the Philippines|National Assembly]] was installed under a new constitution following the passage of the [[Tydings–McDuffie Act]], which established the [[Commonwealth of the Philippines]]. Since the [[1941 Philippine Senate election|1941 elections]], when the Senate was restored after a [[1940 Philippine constitutional plebiscites|constitutional plebiscite]], all twenty-four members of the upper house have been elected countrywide [[at-large]].

== Congressional representation ==
{{main|Agusan del Norte's 1st congressional district|Agusan del Norte's 2nd congressional district}}
Agusan del Norte has been represented in the lower house of [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various Philippine national legislatures]] since 1987, through its [[Agusan del Norte's 1st congressional district|first]] and [[Agusan del Norte's 2nd congressional district|second congressional districts]].

== Provincial board districts ==
{{main|Agusan del Norte Provincial Board}}
The municipalities of Agusan del Norte are represented in the [[Agusan del Norte Provincial Board]], the [[Sangguniang Panlalawigan]] (provincial legislature) of the province, through Agusan del Norte's first and second provincial board districts.
